text:
Alex: Heads up — we're seeing repeated gRPC streaming stalls from model-serving pods across two nodes in us-west-2. Traffic looks normal, but long tails (~10–30s) and stream resets. tcpdump shows a lot of ICMP type=3 code=4 (fragmentation needed) for connections between pods on different AZ nodes.

Alex: tcpdump snippet:```
14:12:23.123456 IP 10.2.3.45.43210 > 10.4.5.67.443: Flags [P.], seq 123:567, ack 987, win 64240, length 444
14:12:23.123457 IP 10.4.5.67 > 10.2.3.45: ICMP 3/4, ip 10.2.3.45 > 10.4.5.67: pmtu 1450
```

Mira: Interesting — sounds exactly like PMTU discovery is hitting a roadblock. Are we seeing VXLAN or ENCAP used on the path? If the overlay is adding ~50 bytes and hosts still on 1500 MTU, DF set on some gRPC payloads cause fragmentation-needed. Can you run `ip -d link show` on both nodes and check vxlan/eni MTU and offloads? Also check `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc` on the nodes.

Alex: Confirmed vxlan overlay between nodes. `ip link` shows vxlan0 mtu 1450 on one host and 1500 on the other (ugh). Also found `net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc = 1` on the node where pmtu wasn't updating.

OpsBot: Rolling update note: kernel 5.10.134 -> 5.10.136 rolled to the AZ yesterday 02:00 UTC, and a CNI restart happened as part of the change. Possible config drift on vxlan MTU when the CNI restarted.

Sam: We also saw instances where VM images had host MTU set to 9001 for EBS perf, but overlay code wasn't adjusting vxlan. If DF is set on the client side (some language runtimes set DF on send), we hit ICMP blackholes when intermediate devices drop ICMP replies. Could be AWS NACL or firewall rate-limiting ICMP.

Jia: I ran a quick PMTU probe: `ping -M do -s 1472 10.4.5.67` -> "Frag needed and DF set". With `-s 1400` it works. So practical MTU <= 1450.

Alex: Temporary mitigation applied: set vxlan0 mtu to 1400 on both hosts and restarted the CNI on the affected nodes. Streams recovered immediately (latency tails gone). Not ideal for throughput but reduces drops.

Mira: Good triage. Next steps: create an infra change to standardize overlay MTU at 1400 across all host templates and bake it into the CNI daemonset so new nodes don't drift. Also add PMTU blackhole detection metric (count of ICMP type3/code4 per node) and an alert when > X/min. I'll open CHG-1127 and assign to netops.

Sam: Could also add a startup check to validate `vxlan mtu <= host_mtu - overhead` and a CNI healthcheck that refuses to advertise higher. Will draft a PR for the CNI daemonset and an admission hook. :thumbsup:

Jia: FYI I saw two noisy EC2 instances that were dropping ICMP (cloudguard agent). Filed a ticket with security to whitelist ICMP for intra-AZ flows.

Alex: Thanks all. Saving the tcpdump and logs to /var/log/diag/1867001234-pmtu and linking to the incident. If anyone wants to reproduce, run the `ping -M do` probe above between the two pod IPs.

Mira: Nice. I'll add a postmortem checklist item: validate PMTU and offload settings after kernel/CNI upgrades. (action: CHG-1127). :white_check_mark:
